body:
Investigation 2026-08-09. Full write-up: workspace `notes/KOBO-ANNOTATIONS-WRITEBACK-INVESTIGATION-2026-08-09.md`.

## The exposure

We advertise CWNG as `reading_services_host` whenever Kobo sync is on (`cps/kobo.py:2143-2154`,
`:2174-2177`), so the device sends annotation traffic to us. `cps/readingservices.py` intercepts
PATCH but proxies BOTH verbs to `https://readingservices.kobo.com` (`:384-385`), and proxies
`checkforchanges` unconditionally (`:389-397`). Kobo's cloud has no knowledge of sideloaded books
and never stores their annotations (help.kobo.com/hc/en-us/articles/29991333812631: "You can only
export annotations from books that have been purchased from Kobo or Kobo Plus").

Nobody has ever looked at what those proxied responses contain.

## Why that might matter — janeczku/calibre-web#2610 (verified directly, not via a pilot)

OPEN since 2022-11-29, 13 comments, still reproducing 2025-07-29. Reporter: "the E-Reader updates
annotations and (presumably) tries to fetch annotations from the Calibre-Web server. The
Calibre-web server doesn't provide anything, and the Kobo E-reader deletes all stored annotations
from the local database." Repro: enable Kobo sync -> sync a book -> annotate -> sync again ->
annotations gone. Confirmed independently on Kobo Elipsa, Forma, Clara HD, Clara BW.

**Important re-reading of that thread.** Stock Calibre-Web does NOT redirect `reading_services_host`
— that is a CWA/CWNG-era behaviour. So for those reporters the annotations GET went to **Kobo's own
cloud**, and it is Kobo's cloud that "doesn't provide anything" for a sideloaded book. The reporter's
attribution to Calibre-Web is their inference and is probably wrong. If that re-reading is right the
exposure is *worse* for us, not better: the destructive answer comes from the upstream we forward to.

**Conditional, not universal.** AStrayByte (2025-02, Clara Color FW 4.41.23145, CW 0.6.24) could not
reproduce. remohoeppli found a workaround that works: remove the book from the sync shelf once
synced — i.e. loss is tied to the book being actively in the sync set. #3316 was proposed as a fix;
one user said it worked, another (ttdu, 2025-07) said it did not.

## Our own exposure — checked, and it looks clean, but the check has a hole

Live household instance: 595 `source='kobo'` rows, **zero with `hidden=1`** — the device has never
sent a `deletedAnnotationIds` batch. Rows accumulate steadily (4 on 2026-05-24, 559 on 2026-07-31,
32 on 2026-08-06) and the May rows are still present in August, which a device wiping on every sync
could not produce.

**The hole:** #2610 describes a *silent local* deletion. If Nickel wipes its own database without
PATCHing the deletion, we would never see it. So "zero hidden rows" is consistent with both "no
loss" and "silent loss", and the accumulation pattern is the stronger evidence, not the hidden count.

## Status

NOT established: that we lose data today. NOT established: #2610's mechanism. What IS established
is that we route a device-authoritative annotation channel to a third party with no knowledge of
these books, and the responses have never been inspected.

## Next step (gates future work)

Capture the actual proxied `GET /annotations` and `checkforchanges` response bodies for a sideloaded
book before anyone implements a server-side answer. Implementing that endpoint is a
data-loss-class change, not a feature-class one — a wrong empty-but-authoritative answer destroys
highlights that, for sideloaded books, exist nowhere else.

## Related: our outreach comment on that thread may now be misleading

`new-usemame` commented on #2610 on 2026-05-19: "The 'where did they go' answer is they were always
on the device", pointing users at the `KoboReader.sqlite` import in v4.0.84. That advice only helps
if the rows are still on the device — and the entire complaint is that Nickel deleted them. Worth
an operator decision on whether a follow-up correction is owed. Do not post one unprompted.

resolution.note:
Containment shipped in #1679 (d7e485d24) and verified live on the deployed instance.

The exposure this finding named is closed: an owned-book annotations GET can no longer reach Nickel's destructive replace trigger, because the trigger itself — POST /api/v3/content/checkforchanges — now filters CWNG-owned content ids out of both the outbound request and the response, and a batch that is entirely owned never contacts Kobo at all.

Root cause, established on hardware (Clara BW 4.45.23792, stock Nickel): nothing was broken in Kobo. checkforchanges -> GET is a replace protocol working as designed — the GET response REPLACES the device's entire local Bookmark set for that book. CWNG lost highlights by sitting in the middle and answering that GET destructively (503) while never authoring the set. The v4.1.36 guard failed for exactly this reason: refusing is one of the destructive answers.

Live verification on the deployed instance (OBSERVED), POST /api/v3/content/checkforchanges with a real session:
  A  owned content id      -> 200 [] , no upstream call in the log
  B  id not in the library -> 401 proxied back from Kobo (Cloudflare, WWW-Authenticate: Bearer)
  C  malformed body        -> 200 [] + 'Not proxying an unrecognized Kobo checkforchanges request'
B is the control that makes A mean something: without it, 200 [] is indistinguishable from a route that returns [] to everything.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED, tracked separately by notes/KOBO-TWO-WAY-ANNOTATION-SYNC-DESIGN.md (#1681):
  - markup/stylus annotations remain unrepresentable. 49 ExtraAnnotationData rows across 6 books on the operator's Libra (35 of them on the two Homer translations). Nothing should author an annotation set for those books; the design gates on ExtraAnnotationData IS NOT NULL, i.e. on the property, not the type.
  - Two-way sync itself is designed and proven feasible on hardware but not implemented. Staged rollout, both gates default off.
  - Nothing here retroactively restores anything already deleted.

title: Kobo annotations GET is proxied to Kobo's cloud — unexamined data-loss exposure (CW #2610)
